newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cement demand growing at 9.0 pct - Ambuja.
newsitem.headline: Indian cement demand growing at 9.0 pct - Ambuja.

text.p: Cement maker Gujarat Ambuja Cements Ltd said Indian cement demand grew at 9.0 percent annually during the six months ended December 31, 1996.

"Contrary to general perception, the demand for cement in the country is growing at a good rate of 9.0 percent (April 1996 to December 1996), which is almost equivalent to the growth in the last year during the same period," it said in a statement.
It was referring to cement analysts' forecasts of a lower growth this year, reflecting a slowdown in the economy.
A cement analyst at a leading investment firm in Bombay said he expected cement demand growth to fall to 5.0-6.0 percent in 1996/97 (April-March).
But Gujarat Ambuja, the country's fourth largest cement maker, said it was bullish on the industry.

"January to May is the peak period for construction activity in the country, and it is expected that the demand for cement will remain good during this period and total demand in the country during 1996-97 (April-March) will be about 10 percent over last year's demand of 69 million tonnes," it said.
